title: Sketch what you can’t describe
principle: If you have a layout in your head and no words for it, draw it on paper and upload a photo. Visual intent that resists language still transfers when Claude can see the sketch.
procedure: When layout is clear in your head but not in words, draw it on paper (boxes + labels are enough).
Photograph in even light; crop to the sketch; upload.
Ask the model to recreate structure/hierarchy/proportions—not invent a new composition.
Gate structural changes behind a question; allow only spacing/type polish without asking.
If the recreation drifts, point-and-talk with a markup on the sketch photo rather than rewriting prose.
examplePrompts: I uploaded a photo of a paper sketch. Recreate this layout structure in HTML—same regions, hierarchy, and proportions. Do not invent a different composition. Ask before changing the structure.
Here is a second photo of the same sketch with red arrows. Keep regions A/B/C exactly; only adjust the gutter between A and B to match the arrow note. Ask before any other structural change.
tips: Use this when you can picture the layout but can’t name it.
The sketch is the brief; the prompt should protect that structure.
Pairs well with wireframe-first when fidelity still doesn’t matter.
Keep Quiet Folio paper/ink if applying on this desk—no purple chrome.
Even box-and-arrow paper beats spatial scavenger-hunt prose.

workedExamples.title: Words fail, boxes win
workedExamples.before: Three paragraphs describing a sidebarish nav with a hero that kind of overlaps.
workedExamples.after: Paper boxes uploaded; HTML regions match proportions; model asks before changing structure.
workedExamples.body: Nate Anthropic blog: draw what you cannot describe, upload the photo. Cite public post.

workedExamples.title: Failure: improve the composition
workedExamples.body: If the prompt invites invention, the sketch becomes moodboarding and you lose the mental model you already had.

antiPatterns: Letting the model “improve” the composition unasked.
Uploading a scribble with no region labels and expecting perfect IA.
checklist: Drift fixed via markup, not a full rewrite.
promptWhy: Photo + “do not invent a different composition” makes the sketch authoritative.
Markup-on-sketch keeps authority with the drawing when the first pass drifts.

Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Sketch what you can’t describe” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
1. When layout is clear in your head but not in words, draw it on paper (boxes + labels are enough).
2. Photograph in even light; crop to the sketch; upload.
3. Ask the model to recreate structure/hierarchy/proportions—not invent a new composition.
4. Gate structural changes behind a question; allow only spacing/type polish without asking.
5. If the recreation drifts, point-and-talk with a markup on the sketch photo rather than rewriting prose.
acceptance: Show the before/after artifact and explain how “Sketch what you can’t describe” improves the named user task.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
